quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-Q: Bitcoin Mining revenue was $25,859 thousand in the three months ended June 30, 2026 versus $55,418 thousand a year earlier (six months $55,752 versus $101,312); energy sales $2,386 versus $2,949, electrical services $2,006 versus $1,006 and cryptocurrency hosting $179 versus $1,535. Bitcoin earned through Bitcoin Mining fell 36% to 354 (556 a year earlier) and 29% to 742 in the six months (1,048); cost per kWh was $0.054 versus $0.053 and Average Watts/Average TH efficiency 19. Year-to-date revenue from continuing operations fell $22.0 million in Canada (lower average Bitcoin price and higher Network Difficulty) and $19.1 million in the United States, which also reflects the April 2026 shutdown of Bitcoin Mining in Washington for the HPC data center build, partly offset by higher energy sales.
quarterly_data.figure: Bitcoin Mining revenue $25,859 thousand (vs $55,418 thousand); 354 Bitcoin earned (-36%)

quarterly_data.signal: Keel's 10-Q: Keel maintains its legacy Bitcoin Mining operations in Canada while working to secure the legal and regulatory approvals to convert its energy purchase agreements in the United States and Canada from Bitcoin Mining to HPC and AI workloads; it sells hashrate to Mining Pool operators under Full Pay Per Share and is paid in Bitcoin daily. The Paso Pe Bitcoin data center in Paraguay was sold on April 21, 2026, and miners classified as held for sale were $13,013 thousand at June 30, 2026 ($166 thousand at December 31, 2025). Bitcoin Mining remained its only reportable segment; it expects to reassess, and may identify a separate HPC reportable segment, once HPC capacity is placed in service under executed customer contracts.
